style.vernacular: Dense metro of flat-roofed reinforced-concrete houses and mid-rise blocks painted in white, cream and tropical pastels, with louvred jalousie windows, iron grilles and carports; Old San Juan has 2-4 storey Spanish colonial townhouses in ochre, salmon, blue and yellow with wooden balconies on blue adoquin cobbles; Hato Rey and Santurce add 1950s-60s tropical-modern slab blocks and glass bank towers.
style.ornament: Spanish colonial wooden and wrought-iron balconies, arched doorways, decorative cement floor tiles, stone garitas (sentry boxes) on the old walls; breeze-block (celosia) screens and jalousie louvres on tropical-modern buildings; Antonin Nechodoma Prairie and Gothic Revival details on early 1900s churches.

sources.what: tropical monsoon climate, Old San Juan fortifications and UNESCO status, hurricane damage to roofs
